title: 2006 AMC 12B Problem 12
statement: The parabola \(y = ax^2 + bx + c\) has vertex \((p, p)\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, -p),\) where \(p \neq 0.\) What is \(b?\)

solutions.text:
The vertex form is \(y = a(x - p)^2 + p.\)

At \(x = 0,\) \(y = ap^2 + p = -p,\) so \(ap^2 = -2p\) and \(a = -\dfrac{2}{p}.\)

Expanding, \(y = a x^2 - 2ap\, x + ap^2 + p,\) so \(b = -2ap = -2\left(-\dfrac{2}{p}\right)p = 4.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Write the parabola in vertex form \(y = a(x - p)^2 + p\)
Use the \(y\)-intercept to find \(a\) in terms of \(p,\) then read off the coefficient of \(x\)
